headline: Council votes to release October 6 executive session minutes on Flock cameras, after public comment on the cameras.
summary: Public speakers asked that the minutes be released in full and that Flock be debated in open session. They also asked that any decision go into police policy 330.08 and the Flock contract. The council also voted to authorize buying 276 Broadway Street for the Senior Center. A tax increment financing agreement with Charles Stock Draper Laboratories Inc. moved to the next agenda after an objection.
decisions: Approved release of October 6 executive session minutes on Flock cameras, 10 yeas.
Moved the Draper Laboratory agreement to the next agenda after an objection under council rule 27.
Approved asking the city clerk to prepare LHA TIF executive session minutes for council and solicitor review before release.
Approved asking the city manager for a report on enforcing approval conditions at the appallorchard project.
Approved asking the city manager to explore a residential tax exemption and a good landlord tax abatement.
Approved asking the finance subcommittee and city finance team to meet as needed for the FY 28 budget process.
Approved asking the council to go into executive session to review unreleased minutes and set a timeline for their release.
Referred Boston gas request to replace a gas main on Westford Street to the wiring inspector.
Referred National Grid request for underground conduit along Robson Street to the wiring inspector.
Referred Zayo request for underground fiber optic conduit at 174 South Street to the wiring inspector.
Approved one out-of-state travel request for DPD, 10 yes votes.
Approved authorizing a plan change to the Acre urban renewal plan for 276 Broadway Street, 10 yes votes.
Approved buying 276 Broadway Street for the Senior Center through a purchase and sales agreement.
Referred Flock camera concerns raised in public comment to the city manager for a report and recommendation.
discussion: Flock minutes and open session: Public speakers asked that the October 6 minutes be released and that any Flock decision be debated in open session. Speakers also said the Flock contract lets the company use customer data.
Flock cameras in public comment: A speaker asked the council to reconsider the cameras, citing AI tracking and data sharing.
Draper agreement objection: An objection under council rule 27 moved the vote to the next agenda. The objection cited a need for community engagement on what is being built nearby.

Bar and restaurant licenses: Council discussed separate restaurant and bar or pub licenses, with the license commission to take up the rules at its November 5th meeting. Questions covered what counts as suitable food and how to verify that food is still served.
